harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (RHEL 7.9), installed Podman, created the unprivileged user appsvc, and configured a rootless container (nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:alpine) running on port 8080 under that account. The container starts at boot via a systemd system unit (webapp-container.service, User=appsvc) that requires no active login session for appsvc - only lingering is enabled, no logind session exists. Verified across a full node restart: new boot ID, container auto-started, and HTTP 200 served on port 8080, all with zero login sessions for appsvc.
actions_performed: Diagnosed RHEL7 node had no configured yum repos/subscription and no internet to standard mirrors; added CentOS 7.9 vault base/updates/extras repos, EPEL via archives.fedoraproject.org, and the kubic libcontainers repo
Fixed a large system clock skew (~34 days) via HTTP Date header + date -s, which was breaking TLS to some mirrors; restarted chronyd afterward
Installed podman 1.6.4 (RHEL7 extras channel) plus dependencies (runc, conmon, fuse-overlayfs, slirp4netns, containernetworking-plugins)
Created unprivileged user appsvc with subuid/subgid ranges; enabled user.max_user_namespaces sysctl (was 0, blocking user namespaces)

Diagnosed and fixed a self-inflicted setuid+file-capability conflict on /usr/bin/newuidmap and /usr/bin/newgidmap (kernel refuses to raise capabilities when both are present) by removing the erroneously added setuid bit, restoring correct multi-line subuid/subgid mapping for rootless podman
Diagnosed a rootless-storage caching issue where podman fell back to single-ID mapping after an earlier failed attempt; fixed by clearing appsvc's container storage state

Diagnosed stock nginx:alpine failing with pwrite() Operation not permitted on its pidfile under rootless podman on this old 3.10 kernel, traced to the OCI default seccomp profile being incompatible with the kernel; switched to nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:alpine with seccomp=unconfined
Created and enabled appsvc account with loginctl enable-linger

Generated and adapted a systemd system unit (webapp-container.service, User=appsvc) since RHEL7's systemd 219 package does not ship user@.service (systemctl --user unsupported), enabling boot start without a login session via RuntimeDirectory=user/1001

Ran the mandatory restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and healthy service/container/HTTP state, restarted node1 via shutdown -r now, polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, and verified container, systemd unit, and HTTP 8080 all recovered with no login session for appsvc

evidence.requirement: Container app runs as unprivileged account appsvc, serving on port 8080
evidence.summary: curl to $NODE_IP:8080 returns HTTP 200 and nginx welcome page; podman ps/systemctl status show the container and its process tree running under appsvc

evidence.requirement: Service starts at boot while appsvc has no active login session
evidence.summary: loginctl shows appsvc has Sessions= empty (only linger) while its podman/conmon/nginx processes are running; systemd unit enabled with WantedBy=multi-user.target and User=appsvc
Captured baseline boot_id (e9250ad1...), systemd enabled/active state, and HTTP 200 response prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Node restarted via native safe mechanism, ack returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now issued in background; connection closed by remote host confirming reboot proceeded

evidence.requirement: Boot identity changed, proving actual restart (not just service restart)
evidence.summary: Post-reboot boot_id is 6ae46876-1f77-452b-b613-4aa67dc85419, differing from baseline e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf, with uptime reset to 0 minutes

evidence.requirement: Service, container, and data recovered post-restart with no login session
evidence.summary: After reboot: systemctl is-enabled/is-active both report enabled/active, container webapp is Up and serving, curl returns HTTP 200, and loginctl confirms appsvc still has zero sessions
